readings.title: The room inside the old station
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: An unused railway waiting room became a small study centre. The first design replaced every original bench with new furniture. Residents suggested keeping two benches because they showed how the room had once been used. The designer retained them along one wall while adding desks with suitable lighting elsewhere. Visitors could recognise the building's history without being asked to study in uncomfortable positions. Reuse involved deciding what should remain and what needed to change.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

readings.title: The window with three comments
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Staff described a renovated office as bright, but afternoon users complained about glare on screens. The facilities team collected comments at several times of day and measured where sunlight fell. Adjustable blinds reduced the glare while allowing daylight when it was useful. The team avoided judging the room from a single morning visit. A comfortable design had to work across changing conditions and for people carrying out different tasks.

readings.title: A door waiting for a home
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: During a hall renovation, workers saved several solid doors for possible reuse. At first they leaned against a wall without labels. Later, a team searching for a matching size had to measure every door again. Volunteers then attached dimensions, condition notes and the place each door had come from. The collection became easier to use. Saving materials avoided immediate disposal, but organised information helped turn a pile of objects into a useful supply.

readings.title: The repair plan in stages
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community centre could not close for an entire renovation because several groups depended on its rooms. The project team divided the work into stages and published which rooms would be available each month. A contact person handled changes when work took longer than expected. The staged approach required extra coordination, but activities continued. The team included this coordination effort in its final report instead of describing uninterrupted service as something that had happened automatically.

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into natural Chinese, preserving its meaning and logical connections.

Giving an old building a new use requires more than preserving its appearance. The space must support the activities that will take place inside it. Some features may tell an important story, while others may prevent comfortable use. Thoughtful renovation makes these choices explicit and explains how the building's past can remain visible within its changing role.
translation.referenceAnswer: 赋予旧建筑新用途，不仅仅是保留其外观。空间必须支持将在其中开展的活动。有些特征可能承载重要的故事，另一些则可能妨碍舒适使用。经过周全考虑的改造会明确这些选择，并解释建筑在角色变化的同时，如何仍让人看见它的过去。
translation.explanation: 参考译文不是唯一答案；信息完整、逻辑准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 words in English for this original simulation task.

A former station waiting room will become an adult study centre. Write a proposal explaining one historical feature to retain, two practical needs to address, and how future users should be consulted.
writing.sampleAnswer: I propose retaining one original bench and a short account of the waiting room's history near the entrance. This would help learners understand the building without making old furniture serve every modern purpose. The main study area needs comfortable desks and lighting that works for reading as well as screens. It also needs a clear route that people with different mobility needs can use. Before final decisions, the project team should invite adult learners to walk through a temporary arrangement and describe any difficulties. Comments should be gathered during both daytime and evening visits because conditions may differ. The finished centre could show which suggestions influenced the design. Reusing the building should preserve a recognisable history while supporting the people who will study there.
writing.explanation: 范文展示一种可行的回应；允许不同观点和例子，按任务完成、组织和语言评分。
